findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the `_criteria_eval` pre-validation guard in `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:144-155` to also accept criterion ids present in `code_review.registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)`, or widen the check to the union of both registries.
evidence: guard code: `if args.criterion_id not in registry.by_id(repo_root):` — uses `plan_review.registry` exclusively
plan Approach section: 'Keep the work limited to the resolver/calibration seam and behavioral tests; do not add project-specific special cases.' — does not name this CLI file as an edit target
plan AC1: 'An activated project code-review criterion resolves and calibrates through the code-review arm' — unreachable via CLI without updating the guard
findings.finding: The CLI handler `_criteria_eval` in `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:144-155` validates `criterion_id` exclusively against `plan_review.registry.by_id(repo_root)`. A code-review project criterion (e.g. `project.foo`) activated only in the code-review overlay will not appear in the plan-review registry, so the guard will reject it with 'unknown criterion' before `calibrate_criterion` is ever called. The plan does not enumerate this CLI consumer as requiring an update.
scenarios: A user runs `rebar criteria eval project.foo` where `project.foo` is only in the code_review overlay; the CLI rejects it as 'unknown criterion' before `calibrate_criterion` is reached.
The AC's happy-path (`calibrate_criterion` is called directly in tests) passes, but the end-to-end CLI path silently remains broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `plan_review`-only guard with a union check: `known = set(plan_review.registry.by_id(repo_root)) | set(code_review.registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)); if args.criterion_id not in known: ...`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify in the Approach whether `calibrate_criterion` accepts logical ids, physical ids, or both for code-review criteria; and specify whether the new predicate must also handle a physical `'code-review-'`-prefixed id (e.g. by stripping the prefix before the `effective_criteria` membership check, or by adding a second predicate `criterion_id.startswith('code-review-')`).
evidence: `effective_criteria` returns `('security', 'performance', ..., 'project.foo')` — logical ids only (confirmed reading registry.py:179-184)
Current `calibrate_criterion` comment says 'a project.<name> criterion's fixture is `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-<name>.eval.yaml`' — physical id oriented

The AC says `_code_review_prompt_id('code-review-project-foo', repo_root=repo_root)` — a physical id — is the test input, but `calibrate_criterion` is driven by `criterion_id` which the plan elsewhere describes as the logical id
The plan does not clarify whether `calibrate_criterion` accepts logical ids, physical ids, or both for code-review criteria
findings.finding: The plan asserts that `calibrate_criterion` in `eval.py` 'maps non-physical ids through the default plan-review namespace' (current behaviour), implying the new code-review arm branches on `criterion_id in code_review.registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)`. However, the current `calibrate_criterion` also reaches `criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id)` for ANY id that doesn't start with `'plan-review-'`, which already includes code-review physical ids like `'code-review-project-foo'`. The plan does not specify whether the new predicate fires on the LOGICAL id (e.g. `'project.foo'`) or on a physical id passed directly. If a caller passes the physical id `'code-review-project-foo'`, `effective_criteria()` returns logical ids only (e.g. `'project.foo'`), so the membership check would MISS it and fall through to the plan-review branch, mapping it as `'plan-review-code-review-project-foo'` — a double-prefixed, broken prompt id.
findings.location: Approach section — 'In `eval.py`, select the new code-review calibration arm with one explicit predicate: `criterion_id in code_review.registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)`'
scenarios: A maintainer calls `calibrate_criterion('code-review-project-foo', repo_root=repo_root)` (physical id, as suggested by AC3) — the `effective_criteria` membership check returns False, the plan-review fallthrough fires, and `criterion_prompt_id('code-review-project-foo')` produces `'plan-review-code-review-project-foo'`, causing a confusing `EvalError` rather than running the code-review calibration arm.
